BETA.description: Beta Labs builds small autonomous delivery drones that navigate urban corridors without a permanent flight corridor, and it publishes its trajectory planner under a permissive licence for academic reuse.

GENEVA.description: Geneva hosts both companies inside its industrial district, and the local university runs the safety certification programme that both of them depend on for cross border shipments of their assembled units.

ZURICH.description: Zurich supplies the precision actuators that both assembly lines fit into their joints, and the supplier audits every batch against the tolerance table before it ships the parts to the two assembly plants.

BETA\u0000GENEVA.description: Beta Labs certifies its drones with the Geneva programme before any unit may leave the district, which adds six weeks to every delivery season and has kept the two rivals out of each other's certified corridors.

cases.name: describe_truncates_and_filters_sub_community_reports
cases.note: Report rows measure 110/149 tokens against the 252-token remaining budget, so the reference keeps only the highest-occurrence row (id 0, 7 tokens of slack) and drops id 1: S000 leaves the Entities CSV with the kept row while S003, covered only by the dropped row, stays; the id `9` has no report and is skipped without a row.

0.title: Trunc first
0.report_string:
# S000 side report

The first sub community secures the certified corridor and inventories every partner that assembles the actuator batches along it, together with the safety milestones the programme cleared before the winter season. It also records the price cuts that narrowed the warehouse accounts twice in the last eighteen months and the delivery routes that both rivals still share under the certification agreement. A closing note lists the suppliers audited against the tolerance table and the batches that failed the joint review earlier this year, which keeps the paragraph growing until it occupies the budget on its own.

1.title: Trunc second
1.report_string:
# S003 side report

The second sub community describes the rival assembly line, the joint audits it runs against the tolerance table, and the delivery season it shares with the certification programme. Its paragraphs repeat the corridor inventory with the same cadence so that the pair of reports, taken together, crosses the remaining budget while either of them alone would still fit beside the entity and relationship rows. The tail row exists only to be dropped: the reference stops the sub community list before it, and the covered node keeps its place in the entity CSV, which is exactly the boundary this case pins. A last sentence pads the row past the boundary with several tokens of slack on both sides, so a couple of tokens of tokenizer drift cannot flip which rows survive.
